note: AD-8: rules whose definitions are sound (validateRuleDefinition → []) or broken (→ at least one problem), as judged by the reference. Fixed data: never edit.

rule.name: Gross salary (B1(i)) = 17(1) + 17(2) + 17(3) + 89A notified country + 89A other country
rule.group: Part B – Salary and other sources (dropdowns)

rule.name: Allowances exempt u/s 10 (B1ii) = sum of the individual exempt allowances
Net salary (B1iii) = gross salary (B1i) − allowances exempt u/s 10 (B1ii) − relief u/s 89A (B1iia)
rule.notes: Income claimed for relief u/s 89A (B1iia) is also subtracted, as per the form (iii = i − ii − iia).

rule.name: Standard deduction u/s 16(ia) ≤ lower of Rs 50,000 and net salary
rule.notes: "Total salary" read as net salary (B1iii), the amount from which the deduction is made.

rule.name: Deductions u/s 16 (B1 iv) = standard deduction + entertainment allowance + professional tax
Income chargeable under Salaries (B1v) = net salary (B1iii) − deductions u/s 16 (B1iv)
Annual value (B2iii) = gross rent (B2i) − tax paid to local authorities (B2ii)
Standard deduction (B2iv) = 30% of annual value (B2iii)
rule.notes: A negative annual value gives no 30% deduction.

rule.name: Income under House Property (B2vii) = B2iii − B2iv − B2v + B2vi
Income from other sources (B3) = sum of the individual other-source incomes
Deduction u/s 57(iia) only when family pension is offered under other sources
rule.notes: Family pension = other-sources rows with nature FAP.

rule.name: Deduction u/s 57(iia) ≤ lower of 1/3rd of family pension and Rs 15,000
rule.notes: +1 rounding allowance on the one-third.

rule.name: Old regime: gross total income = salary + house property + other sources
rule.notes: Other sources taken net of deduction u/s 57(iia) and relief u/s 89A (the two "Less" lines under B3), because B3 itself is the gross dropdown total (Sl. 40).

rule.name: Default (new) regime with house property loss: gross total income = salary + other sources (loss ignored)
rule.notes: Loss under house property cannot be set off against other heads u/s 115BAC. Other sources net of 57(iia) and 89A relief (see Sl. 7).

rule.name: Default (new) regime with positive house property income: gross total income = salary + house property + other sources
rule.notes: Other sources net of 57(iia) and 89A relief (see Sl. 7).

rule.name: Exempt income total = sum of the individual exempt incomes
80D: preventive health check-up (all four fields together) ≤ Rs 5,000
80D 1a = health insurance premium (i) + preventive check-up (ii), capped at Rs 25,000
rule.notes: The cap is folded into the equality so an above-cap break-up with a capped 1a passes.

rule.name: 80D 1b (self & family, senior citizen) ≤ Rs 50,000
80D 1b = premium (i) + check-up (ii) + medical expenditure (iii), capped at Rs 50,000
80D 2a (parents) ≤ Rs 25,000
80D 2a = premium (i) + preventive check-up (ii), capped at Rs 25,000
80D 2b (parents, senior citizen) ≤ Rs 50,000
80D 2b = premium (i) + check-up (ii) + medical expenditure (iii), capped at Rs 50,000
rule.notes: The document checks the equality only below Rs 50,000; folding the cap into min() is equivalent.

rule.name: 80D 3 eligible amount ≤ Rs 1,00,000
80D 3 eligible amount = 1a + 1b + 2a + 2b, capped at Rs 1,00,000 and at gross total income
Deduction u/s 80GGC in Part C = eligible amount of contribution in Schedule 80GGC
rule.notes: Old regime only (s.115BAC(2)); see rule Aderived80GGC-sch.

rule.name: 80GGC: eligible amount per row = lower of contribution in other mode and gross total income
80GGC: total contribution = contribution in cash + contribution in other mode
80GGC: total eligible amount = sum of the rows’ eligible amounts, restricted to gross total income
Total of deductions claimed (user block) = sum of the individual claimed amounts
rule.notes: UsrDeductUndChapVIA holds the amounts as typed; its total is a plain sum (the GTI restriction applies to DeductUndChapVIA, Sl. 112).

rule.name: Deductions u/s 80C + 80CCC + 80CCD(1) ≤ Rs 1,50,000
Deduction u/s 80TTA ≤ Rs 10,000
Deduction u/s 80TTA ≤ interest from savings account under other sources
rule.notes: Savings interest = other-sources rows with nature SAV.

rule.name: Senior citizen cannot claim deduction u/s 80TTA (80TTB applies instead)
rule.notes: Senior = 60 or more during FY 2023-24, i.e. DOB on or before 1964-04-01 (the document's "on or after 02.04.1964" is the non-senior side).

rule.name: Deduction u/s 80TTB ≤ Rs 50,000
Deduction u/s 80TTB only for senior citizens (DOB on or before 1964-04-01)
Total Chapter VI-A deductions (B5) = sum of the individual deductions, restricted to gross total income
Total income = Gross total income − total Chapter VI-A deductions (not below zero)
rule.notes: Tolerance ±5: total income is rounded to the nearest Rs 10 (s.288A).

rule.name: Total income cannot exceed Rs 50 lakh in ITR-1
Old regime: rebate u/s 87A not available when total income exceeds Rs 5,00,000
Old regime: rebate u/s 87A cannot exceed Rs 12,500 (nor the tax payable)
rule.notes: The rebate is also capped at the tax payable on total income (D1) since it cannot create a negative tax.

rule.name: New regime: rebate u/s 87A above Rs 7,00,000 limited to marginal relief (tax − excess income over 7 lakh)
rule.notes: Marginal rebate (proviso to s.87A): when total income exceeds 7 lakh the rebate cannot exceed tax payable minus the excess of income over 7 lakh; beyond ~7.28 lakh this forces the rebate to zero.

rule.name: New regime: rebate u/s 87A cannot exceed Rs 25,000 (nor the tax payable)
Tax after rebate (D3) = tax payable on total income (D1) − rebate u/s 87A (D2)
Health & education cess (D4) = 4% of tax after rebate (D3)
rule.notes: Derived from the form: ITR-1 has no surcharge, so cess is 4% of D3 (±1 for rounding).

rule.name: Total tax and cess (D5) = tax after rebate (D3) + health & education cess (D4)
Balance tax after relief (D7) = total tax and cess (D5) − relief u/s 89 (D6)
rule.notes: Derived from the form arithmetic; together with Sl. 15 and Sl. 66 this keeps D5–D9 consistent.

rule.name: Total interest and fee payable (D8) = 234A + 234B + 234C + 234F
Total tax, fee and interest (D9) = D5 + 234A + 234B + 234C + 234F − relief u/s 89 (D6)
Total tax, fee and interest (D9) = balance tax after relief (D7) + total interest and fee (D8)
No late filing fee u/s 234F when the return is filed within the due date (139(1))
Late filing fee u/s 234F cannot exceed Rs 5,000 (Rs 1,000 when total income ≤ Rs 5 lakh)
Schedule IT: total tax paid = sum of col 4 of all challans
rule.group: Schedules IT / TDS / TCS – Taxes paid details

rule.name: Schedule TDS1: total tax deducted = sum of the rows
rule.group: Schedules IT / TDS / TCS – Taxes paid details

rule.name: Schedule TDS2: total TDS credit claimed this year (col 6) = sum of the rows
rule.group: Schedules IT / TDS / TCS – Taxes paid details

rule.name: Schedule TDS3: total TDS credit claimed this year (col 6) = sum of the rows
rule.group: Schedules IT / TDS / TCS – Taxes paid details

rule.name: Schedule TCS: total TCS credit claimed this year (col 6) = sum of the rows
rule.group: Schedules IT / TDS / TCS – Taxes paid details

rule.name: Advance tax (D10a) = Schedule IT payments dated 01-04-2023 to 31-03-2024
rule.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rule.name: Self-assessment tax (D10d) = Schedule IT payments dated after 31-03-2024
rule.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rule.name: TDS claimed (D10b) = total TDS claimed in Schedules TDS1 + TDS2 + TDS3
rule.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rule.name: TCS claimed (D10c) = total TCS claimed in Schedule TCS
rule.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rule.name: Total taxes paid (D10) = advance tax + TDS + TCS + self-assessment tax
rule.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rule.name: Total taxes paid (D10) = Schedule IT + TDS1 + TDS2 + TDS3 + TCS totals
rule.notes: The scenario text lists IT, TDS1, TDS2 and TCS; Schedule TDS3 (Form 26QC) is also part of the TDS claimed in ITR-1 and is included so that the totals reconcile.
rule.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rule.name: Refund (D12) = total taxes paid (D10) − total tax, fee and interest (D9), when positive
rule.notes: Refund is 0 (not negative) when taxes paid fall short of the liability. Tolerance ±5: the refund is rounded to the nearest Rs 10 (s.288B).
rule.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rule.name: Amount payable (D11) = total tax, fee and interest (D9) − total taxes paid (D10), when positive
rule.notes: Amount payable is 0 (not negative) when taxes paid exceed the liability. Tolerance ±5: the amount is rounded to the nearest Rs 10 (s.288B).
rule.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rule.name: Schedule IT: a challan for AY 2024-25 cannot be dated before 01-04-2023
rule.notes: Implied by Sl. 205/206: a payment dated before the previous year is neither advance tax nor self-assessment tax, so Sl. 198 (D10 = Schedule IT + TDS + TCS) could not hold.
rule.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rule.name: PAN must be an individual PAN (4th character P) – ITR-1 is for individuals only
rule.notes: The "role CD" of the PAN is its 4th character (P = individual). Full role check against the PAN master is external.

rule.name: IFSC must be in the RBI format (4 letters, 0, 6 alphanumerics)
rule.notes: Partial: matching against the RBI IFSC master needs external data; only the format is checked offline.
rule.group: Part D – Taxes paid and refund

rule.name: Other sources: "Interest from savings bank account" cannot be selected more than once
rule.notes: Dropdown code SAV; the condition restricts the uniqueness check to that code so "OTH" rows may repeat.
rule.group: Part B – Salary and other sources (dropdowns)

rule.name: Other sources: "Interest from deposits (bank / post office / co-operative society)" cannot be selected more than once
rule.notes: Dropdown code IFD; the condition restricts the uniqueness check to that code so "OTH" rows may repeat.
rule.group: Part B – Salary and other sources (dropdowns)

rule.name: Schedule TDS2: TDS claimed this year (col 6) cannot exceed tax deducted (col 5)
rule.group: Schedules IT / TDS / TCS – Taxes paid details

rule.name: PAN in verification must equal the assessee PAN when verifying as Self
